+# Exact transition count of machine 3626
+
+## Abstract
+
+The signed Moebius and totient divisor sum counts every transition of the one-sided machine on every positive binary input.
+
+The external question is Peter Bala's conjecture in OEIS A393210, also recorded in A069517; the alias pair is one question. Its unchanged prospective registration is https://github.com/the-omega-institute/trureturing/issues/25808#issuecomment-6587694551. The scope is every positive natural input, with no finite cutoff, tape bound or counter width.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (Two machine states).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S0/Computability/BinaryMachine/Machine3626.State`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S0/Computability/BinaryMachine/Machine3626.State` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Peter Bala; Sean A. Irvine; Stephen Wolfram (2026). *OEIS A393210: halting time for Wolfram machine 3626*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A393210>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+State has exactly the constructors A and B; termination is a boundary crossing, rather than a third state.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (Unbounded half-tape configuration).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S0/Computability/BinaryMachine/Machine3626.Cfg`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S0/Computability/BinaryMachine/Machine3626.Cfg` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Peter Bala; Sean A. Irvine; Stephen Wolfram (2026). *OEIS A393210: halting time for Wolfram machine 3626*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A393210>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Cfg contains state : State, left : List Bool, and right : List Bool. The head scans the first left bit. Absent left bits are implicit blank zero. The right list records cells between the head and the fixed right boundary. Both list lengths are unbounded.
+
+**Definition 1.3 (Right move and boundary crossing).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S0/Computability/BinaryMachine/Machine3626.exitRight`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S0/Computability/BinaryMachine/Machine3626.exitRight` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Peter Bala; Sean A. Irvine; Stephen Wolfram (2026). *OEIS A393210: halting time for Wolfram machine 3626*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A393210>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For writtenLeft : List Bool and right : List Bool, exitRight writtenLeft [] is none. For right = b :: rest it is some (Cfg.mk State.B (b :: writtenLeft) rest). This consumes the nearest right cell and enters B after writing; none denotes the actual boundary crossing.
+
+**Definition 1.4 (Literal transition semantics).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S0/Computability/BinaryMachine/Machine3626.step`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S0/Computability/BinaryMachine/Machine3626.step` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Peter Bala; Sean A. Irvine; Stephen Wolfram (2026). *OEIS A393210: halting time for Wolfram machine 3626*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A393210>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Cfg has a state A or B and two unbounded Boolean lists. The left list begins at the scanned cell and continues toward the most significant end; absent cells are implicit blank zero. The right list records the finite distance to the fixed right boundary. The four simultaneous read/write/state/move rules are A0 to A0L, A1 to B1R, B0 to A1L, and B1 to B0R. exitRight returns none precisely when a right move crosses the boundary; otherwise its result has state B. There is no separate halt state.
+
+**Definition 1.5 (Counted first boundary crossing).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S0/Computability/BinaryMachine/Machine3626.Trace`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S0/Computability/BinaryMachine/Machine3626.Trace` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Peter Bala; Sean A. Irvine; Stephen Wolfram (2026). *OEIS A393210: halting time for Wolfram machine 3626*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A393210>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Trace.zero counts zero transitions at a configuration. Trace.cons adds one nonhalting transition to a trace from its successor. Trace.crossing counts exactly one transition whose result is none. No constructor continues a trace after none, so Trace t c none records the first boundary crossing at transition t, rather than merely a visit to a terminal state.
+
+**Definition 1.6 (Positive binary input at the right edge).**
+
+$$\forall n: \mathbb{N}, \operatorname{initial}\left(n\right) = \operatorname{Cfg}.\operatorname{mk}\left(\operatorname{State}.\operatorname{A}, \operatorname{Nat}.\operatorname{bits}\left(n\right), \operatorname{List}.\operatorname{nil}\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S0/Computability/BinaryMachine/Machine3626.initial` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Peter Bala; Sean A. Irvine; Stephen Wolfram (2026). *OEIS A393210: halting time for Wolfram machine 3626*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A393210>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Nat.bits is least-significant-bit first. The head scans that bit in state A at the right boundary; the empty right list fixes the actual boundary. Blank cells extend infinitely to the left of the most significant digit. The final result excludes n = 0.
+
+**Definition 1.7 (Zeros before the first one).**
+
+$$\forall k: \mathbb{N}, \forall higher: \operatorname{List}\left(Bool\right), \operatorname{block}\left(k, higher\right) = \operatorname{List}.\operatorname{append}\left(\operatorname{List}.\operatorname{replicate}\left(k, false\right), \operatorname{List}.\operatorname{cons}\left(true, higher\right)\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S0/Computability/BinaryMachine/Machine3626.block` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Peter Bala; Sean A. Irvine; Stephen Wolfram (2026). *OEIS A393210: halting time for Wolfram machine 3626*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A393210>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The block contains k zero bits followed by its first one and arbitrary higher bits. The lists have no fixed maximum length.
+
+**Theorem 1.8 (A restoring block crosses in the exact count).**
+
+$$\forall k: \mathbb{N}, \forall higher: \operatorname{List}\left(Bool\right), \operatorname{Trace}\left(4 \cdot 2^{k} - 3, \operatorname{Cfg}.\operatorname{mk}\left(\operatorname{State}.\operatorname{A}, \operatorname{block}\left(k, higher\right), \operatorname{List}.\operatorname{nil}\right), none\right)$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S0/Computability/BinaryMachine/Machine3626.block_first_crossing` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Peter Bala; Sean A. Irvine; Stephen Wolfram (2026). *OEIS A393210: halting time for Wolfram machine 3626*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A393210>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The recursive trace restores the lower block after each of two smaller traversals and then exits. Its transition count satisfies T(0) = 1 and T(k+1) = 2 T(k) + 3. Solving this recurrence gives 4 times 2 to the k minus 3. Higher cells remain arbitrary. The last crossing transition is included.
+
+**Theorem 1.9 (Every positive input has the required operational trace).**
+
+$$\forall n: \mathbb{N}, 0 < n \Rightarrow \exists k: \mathbb{N}, \exists higher: \operatorname{List}\left(Bool\right), \operatorname{Nat}.\operatorname{bits}\left(n\right) = \operatorname{block}\left(k, higher\right) \land \operatorname{Trace}\left(4 \cdot 2^{k} - 3, \operatorname{initial}\left(n\right), none\right)$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S0/Computability/BinaryMachine/Machine3626.positive_input_first_crossing` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Peter Bala; Sean A. Irvine; Stephen Wolfram (2026). *OEIS A393210: halting time for Wolfram machine 3626*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A393210>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Binary recursion finds the first one of every positive input. The restoring-block trace then supplies the actual first boundary crossing. This operational theorem is a live prerequisite of the exact arithmetic result.
+
+**Theorem 1.10 (Exact signed Moebius and totient formula).**
+
+$$\forall n: \mathbb{N}, 0 < n \Rightarrow \exists t: \mathbb{N}, \operatorname{Trace}\left(t, \operatorname{initial}\left(n\right), none\right) \land (t: \mathbb{Z}) = \sum_{d \in \operatorname{Nat}.\operatorname{divisors}\left(n\right)} (\sum_{e \in \operatorname{Nat}.\operatorname{divisors}\left(d\right)} (0 - 1)^{e + 1} \cdot \operatorname{ArithmeticFunction}.\operatorname{moebius}\left(e\right))^{2} \cdot (\operatorname{Nat}.\operatorname{totient}\left(d\right): \mathbb{Z})$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S0/Computability/BinaryMachine/Machine3626.result` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Resolves.* `Problems/bala-machine3626-exact-halting-time` (proved) by `D5/S0/Computability/BinaryMachine/Machine3626.result`.
+
+<!-- scribe-open-problem-resolution-v1 {"problem_slug":"bala-machine3626-exact-halting-time","declaration_gid":"D5/S0/Computability/BinaryMachine/Machine3626.result","resolution_kind":"proved"} -->

+
+*Acknowledgement.* Peter Bala; Sean A. Irvine; Stephen Wolfram (2026). *OEIS A393210: halting time for Wolfram machine 3626*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A393210>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The source sentence is: Conjecture: a(n) = Sum_{d | n} m(d)^2 * phi(d), where m(n) = Sum_{d | n} (-1)^(d+1) * moebius(d) = A069517(n) and phi(n) denotes Euler's totient function A000010(n). Cf. A296306. This is the conjecture line in OEIS A393210, revision 18. For every natural n greater than zero there exists a transition count t with Trace t (initial n) none and the displayed integer equality. Both divisor sums range over all positive divisors; powers of minus one, Moebius values, the square and the outer sum are interpreted in the integers. The totient and the natural transition count are cast to integers. The proof uses the published arithmetic multiplicativity and prime-power values through pinned Mathlib's Moebius and totient results. Odd prime factors contribute one to the outer divisor transform; the 2-power factor contributes 4 times 2 to the k minus 3, matching the same binary prefix used by the operational trace. This is a symbolic theorem for all positive inputs. It makes no claim for input zero or for another machine or boundary convention.
+

+   generality: G
+   mirror-B: D5/B/S0/Computability/BinaryMachine/Machine3626
+   mirror-E: none(waiver:external-open-problem-resolution)

+   utility: none

+
+module
+
+public import Mathlib.NumberTheory.ArithmeticFunction.Moebius
+public import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Totient
+
+/-!
+# Exact halting formula for the one-sided two-state machine
+
+Admission basis: open-problem-resolution, preregistered issue #25808.
+The arithmetic prime-power identities are literature-attested in A069517.
+They are consumed here, rather than delivered as separate known results.
+
+Proof shapes and live consumers (same-delivery helpers are inlined):
+* trace_trans: content; consumed by block_trace.
+* block_trace: content; restoring recursion consumed by block_first_crossing.
+* block_first_crossing: content; consumed by positive_input_first_crossing.
+* positive_input_first_crossing: content; consumed by result.
+* signedMu_mult: bind-only; consumed by mass_mult.
+* mass_mult: bind-only; consumed by cost_mult, cost_two_pow, cost_odd_prime_pow.
+* cost_mult: bind-only; consumed by cost_odd and cost_binary_block.
+* mass_prime_pow: bind-only; consumed by cost_two_pow and cost_odd_prime_pow.
+* cost_two_pow: bind-only; consumed by cost_binary_block.
+* cost_odd_prime_pow: bind-only; consumed by cost_odd.
+* cost_odd: bind-only; consumed by cost_binary_block.
+* cost_binary_block: bind-only; consumed by result.
+* block_prefix_unique: bind-only; consumed by result.
+* result: content through the live restoring trace; settling result.
+All direct frozen D5 dependencies are absent; pinned Mathlib is used directly.
+No arithmetic helper supplies an independent escape witness.
+-/
+
+set_option autoImplicit false
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+namespace D5.S0.Computability.BinaryMachine.Machine3626
+
+inductive State
+  | A | B
+
+/-- The left list starts at the scanned cell; absent cells are blank zero.
+The right list ends at the fixed right boundary. Both lists have unbounded length. -/
+structure Cfg where
+  state : State
+  left : List Bool
+  right : List Bool
+
+/-- Write at the current cell and move one cell right; crossing the boundary halts. -/
+def exitRight (writtenLeft right : List Bool) : Option Cfg :=
+  match right with
+  | [] => none
+  | b :: rest => some ⟨.B, b :: writtenLeft, rest⟩
+
+/-- Each application is one simultaneous read/write/state-change/move transition.
+The two empty-left cases read an implicit blank cell on the infinite half-tape. -/
+def step : Cfg → Option Cfg
+  | ⟨.A, [], right⟩ => some ⟨.A, [], false :: right⟩
+  | ⟨.A, false :: left, right⟩ => some ⟨.A, left, false :: right⟩
+  | ⟨.A, true :: left, right⟩ => exitRight (true :: left) right
+  | ⟨.B, [], right⟩ => some ⟨.A, [], true :: right⟩
+  | ⟨.B, false :: left, right⟩ => some ⟨.A, left, true :: right⟩
+  | ⟨.B, true :: left, right⟩ => exitRight (false :: left) right
+
+/-- A trace may stop at its current configuration or at the first boundary crossing.
+There is no constructor that continues after a crossing; the crossing counts one step. -/
+inductive Trace : ℕ → Cfg → Option Cfg → Prop
+  | zero (c : Cfg) : Trace 0 c (some c)
+  | cons {t : ℕ} {c d : Cfg} {result : Option Cfg}
+      (transition : step c = some d) (rest : Trace t d result) :
+      Trace (t + 1) c result
+  | crossing {c : Cfg} (transition : step c = none) : Trace 1 c none
+
+private theorem trace_trans {s t : ℕ} {c : Cfg} {endpoint result : Option Cfg}
+    (h : Trace s c endpoint) :
+    ∀ {d : Cfg}, endpoint = some d → Trace t d result → Trace (s + t) c result := by
+  induction h with
+  | zero c =>
+    intro d he j
+    cases he
+    simpa using j
+  | cons transition rest ih =>
+    intro d he j
+    simpa [Nat.add_assoc, Nat.add_comm, Nat.add_left_comm] using
+      Trace.cons transition (ih he j)
+  | crossing transition =>
+    intro d he
+    cases he
+
+/-- A zero block followed by its first one and arbitrary higher cells. -/
+def block (k : ℕ) (higher : List Bool) : List Bool :=
+  List.replicate k false ++ true :: higher
+
+private def blockTime : ℕ → ℕ
+  | 0 => 1
+  | k + 1 => 2 * blockTime k + 3
+
+private theorem block_trace (k : ℕ) (higher right : List Bool) :
+    Trace (blockTime k) ⟨.A, block k higher, right⟩
+      (exitRight (block k higher) right) := by
+  induction k generalizing right with
+  | zero =>
+    cases right with
+    | nil => exact Trace.crossing rfl
+    | cons b rest => exact Trace.cons rfl (Trace.zero _)
+  | succ k ih =>
+    have hleft : Trace (blockTime k) ⟨.A, block k higher, false :: right⟩
+        (some ⟨.B, false :: block k higher, right⟩) := by
+      simpa [exitRight] using ih (false :: right)
+    have hright : Trace (blockTime k) ⟨.A, block k higher, true :: right⟩
+        (some ⟨.B, true :: block k higher, right⟩) := by
+      simpa [exitRight] using ih (true :: right)
+    have hlast : Trace 1 ⟨.B, true :: block k higher, right⟩
+        (exitRight (false :: block k higher) right) := by
+      cases right with
+      | nil => exact Trace.crossing rfl
+      | cons b rest => exact Trace.cons rfl (Trace.zero _)
+    have hmiddle := trace_trans hleft rfl
+      (Trace.cons (by rfl) (trace_trans hright rfl hlast))
+    have hfull := Trace.cons (c := ⟨.A, false :: block k higher, right⟩)
+      (by rfl) hmiddle
+    simpa [blockTime, block, List.replicate_succ, Nat.two_mul, Nat.add_assoc] using hfull
+
+/-- Every zero block followed by one crosses the actual right boundary for the first time
+in exactly the stated number of transitions, independently of all higher cells. -/
+theorem block_first_crossing (k : ℕ) (higher : List Bool) :
+    Trace (4 * 2 ^ k - 3) ⟨.A, block k higher, []⟩ none := by
+  have htime : ∀ j, blockTime j + 3 = 4 * 2 ^ j := by
+    intro j
+    induction j with
+    | zero => rfl
+    | succ j ih => simp only [blockTime, Nat.pow_succ]; omega
+  have ht : blockTime k = 4 * 2 ^ k - 3 := by have := htime k; omega
+  simpa only [ht, exitRight] using block_trace k higher []
+
+/-- Binary input is least-significant-bit first, with the head at the right edge. -/
+def initial (n : ℕ) : Cfg := ⟨.A, n.bits, []⟩
+
+/-- Every positive binary input has a first one. Its distance from the edge determines
+an actual first-crossing trace, with no bound on the input or the tape. -/
+theorem positive_input_first_crossing (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
+    ∃ (k : ℕ) (higher : List Bool), n.bits = block k higher ∧
+      Trace (4 * 2 ^ k - 3) (initial n) none := by
+  have hshape : ∀ m : ℕ, m ≠ 0 → ∃ (k : ℕ) (higher : List Bool),
+      m.bits = block k higher := by
+    intro m
+    induction m using Nat.binaryRec' with
+    | zero =>
+      intro h
+      exact (h rfl).elim
+    | bit b m hb ih =>
+      intro hm
+      cases b with
+      | true =>
+        exact ⟨0, m.bits, by simp [block]⟩
+      | false =>
+        have hm0 : m ≠ 0 := by
+          intro h
+          simpa using hb h
+        obtain ⟨k, higher, hk⟩ := ih hm0
+        refine ⟨k + 1, higher, ?_⟩
+        rw [Nat.bits_append_bit m false hb, hk]
+        simp [block, List.replicate_succ]
+  obtain ⟨k, higher, hk⟩ := hshape n (Nat.ne_of_gt hn)
+  refine ⟨k, higher, hk, ?_⟩
+  simpa only [initial, hk] using block_first_crossing k higher
+
+open scoped ArithmeticFunction.zeta BigOperators
+open ArithmeticFunction
+
+private def signedMu : ArithmeticFunction ℤ :=
+  ⟨fun n => (-1 : ℤ) ^ (n + 1) * moebius n, by simp⟩
+
+private def mass : ArithmeticFunction ℤ := (ζ : ArithmeticFunction ℤ) * signedMu
+
+private def tot : ArithmeticFunction ℤ :=
+  ⟨fun n => (Nat.totient n : ℤ), by simp⟩
+
+private def cost : ArithmeticFunction ℤ :=
+  (ζ : ArithmeticFunction ℤ) * ((mass.ppow 2).pmul tot)
+
+private theorem signedMu_mult : signedMu.IsMultiplicative := by
+  refine ⟨by norm_num [signedMu], ?_⟩
+  intro a b hab
+  change (-1 : ℤ) ^ (a * b + 1) * moebius (a * b) =
+    ((-1 : ℤ) ^ (a + 1) * moebius a) * ((-1 : ℤ) ^ (b + 1) * moebius b)
+  rw [isMultiplicative_moebius.map_mul_of_coprime hab]
+  have hp : (-1 : ℤ) ^ (a * b + 1) = (-1 : ℤ) ^ (a + 1) * (-1 : ℤ) ^ (b + 1) := by
+    have hnot : ¬ (2 ∣ a ∧ 2 ∣ b) := by
+      rintro ⟨ha, hb⟩
+      have := Nat.dvd_gcd ha hb
+      rw [hab.gcd_eq_one] at this
+      norm_num at this
+    rw [neg_one_pow_eq_pow_mod_two (a * b + 1),
+      neg_one_pow_eq_pow_mod_two (a + 1), neg_one_pow_eq_pow_mod_two (b + 1)]
+    have ha := Nat.mod_lt a (by omega : 0 < 2)
+    have hb := Nat.mod_lt b (by omega : 0 < 2)
+    simp only [Nat.dvd_iff_mod_eq_zero] at hnot
+    rcases Nat.mod_two_eq_zero_or_one a with ha | ha <;>
+      rcases Nat.mod_two_eq_zero_or_one b with hb | hb <;>
+      simp [Nat.add_mod, Nat.mul_mod, ha, hb] at *
+  rw [hp]
+  ring
+
+private theorem mass_mult : mass.IsMultiplicative :=
+  isMultiplicative_zeta.natCast.mul signedMu_mult
+
+private theorem cost_mult : cost.IsMultiplicative :=
+  isMultiplicative_zeta.natCast.mul
+    ((mass_mult.ppow).pmul ⟨by simp [tot], by
+      intro a b hab
+      change (Nat.totient (a * b) : ℤ) = (Nat.totient a : ℤ) * Nat.totient b
+      rw [Nat.totient_mul hab, Nat.cast_mul]⟩)
+
+private theorem mass_prime_pow (p k : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hk : 0 < k) :
+    mass (p ^ k) = 1 - (-1 : ℤ) ^ (p + 1) := by
+  rw [mass, coe_zeta_mul_apply, Nat.sum_divisors_prime_pow hp]
+  rw [Finset.sum_range_succ']
+  simp only [pow_zero]
+  have hterm : ∀ j : ℕ, signedMu (p ^ (j + 1)) =
+      if j = 0 then -(-1 : ℤ) ^ (p + 1) else 0 := by
+    intro j
+    simp only [signedMu, ArithmeticFunction.coe_mk,
+      moebius_apply_prime_pow hp (by omega : j + 1 ≠ 0)]
+    by_cases hj : j = 0
+    · simp [hj]
+    · simp [hj]
+  simp_rw [hterm]
+  simp [signedMu, Finset.sum_ite_eq', hk, sub_eq_add_neg, add_comm]
+
+private theorem cost_two_pow (k : ℕ) : cost (2 ^ k) = 4 * (2 : ℤ) ^ k - 3 := by
+  have ht := congrArg (fun x : ℕ => (x : ℤ)) (Nat.sum_totient (2 ^ k))
+  rw [Nat.sum_divisors_prime_pow Nat.prime_two, Finset.sum_range_succ'] at ht
+  push_cast at ht
+  rw [cost, coe_zeta_mul_apply, Nat.sum_divisors_prime_pow Nat.prime_two,
+    Finset.sum_range_succ']
+  simp only [ArithmeticFunction.pmul_apply, ArithmeticFunction.ppow_apply (by norm_num : 0 < 2)]
+  simp_rw [mass_prime_pow 2 _ Nat.prime_two (Nat.succ_pos _)]
+  norm_num [tot, mass_mult.map_one] at *
+  rw [← Finset.mul_sum]
+  linarith
+
+private theorem cost_odd_prime_pow (p k : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hp2 : p ≠ 2) :
+    cost (p ^ k) = 1 := by
+  have hs : (-1 : ℤ) ^ (p + 1) = 1 := by
+    exact (hp.odd_of_ne_two hp2).add_one.neg_one_pow

+## Exact question
+
+OEIS A393210, revision 18, records Peter Bala's conjecture of September 11,
+2026. The sequence has offset 1 and names Wolfram's two-state two-symbol
+machine 3626. A069517, revision 31, records the same question with the two
+sides interchanged. These records describe one question.

+The source conjecture line in A393210 is:
+
+> Conjecture: a(n) = Sum_{d | n} m(d)^2 * phi(d), where m(n) = Sum_{d | n} (-1)^(d+1) * moebius(d) = A069517(n) and phi(n) denotes Euler's totient function A000010(n). Cf. A296306.

+The arithmetic prerequisites are published in A069517: multiplicativity
+and the values 2 on positive powers of 2 and 0 on positive powers of odd
+primes. The signed sum has value 1 at 1. These are reused arithmetic
+facts, not independent discoveries of this formalization.

+left, initially blank beyond the most significant binary digit. The least
+significant bit and initial state A are at the right boundary. The rules
+are A0 → A0L, A1 → B1R, B0 → A1L, B1 → B0R. Crossing that boundary to the
+right terminates the run; the crossing transition counts. Input zero is
+excluded. An absent list cell in the formal tape denotes an implicit
+blank zero, not a tape bound. No machine step consults an arithmetic
+runtime, simulation cutoff or fixed-width counter.

+# The exact halting time of Wolfram machine 3626
+
+## Problem
+
+Peter Bala, OEIS A393210, conjecture of September 11, 2026, revision 18:
+
+> Conjecture: a(n) = Sum_{d | n} m(d)^2 * phi(d), where m(n) = Sum_{d | n} (-1)^(d+1) * moebius(d) = A069517(n) and phi(n) denotes Euler's totient function A000010(n). Cf. A296306.
+
+The sequence has offset 1. The equivalent conjectural relation in A069517,
+revision 31, is the same question, counted once. Here a(n) is the actual
+number of transitions of the one-sided two-state two-symbol machine 3626
+on every positive natural input n in binary. Its half-tape extends
+infinitely leftward, blank zero beyond the most significant bit. The head
+starts in state A at the right edge on the least significant bit. Its
+rules are A0 → A0L, A1 → B1R, B0 → A1L, B1 → B0R. A simultaneous read,
+write, state change and move counts as one transition. Moving right off
+the edge terminates the run, and that final transition is counted.
+Input zero is excluded. There is no time cap, tape bound or counter width.
+Both divisor sums range over positive divisors; the signed Moebius
+arithmetic is in the integers.
+
+## Motivation
+
+`D5/S0/Computability/BinaryMachine/Machine3626.result` supplies an actual
+first-boundary-crossing trace for every n > 0 whose natural transition
+count, cast to the integers, equals the source's signed Moebius/totient
+sum. Operational execution is defined independently of the arithmetic
+formula. The literal source, published arithmetic prerequisites and
+primary machine-number decoder are cited in
+`Library/Computability/bala2026machine3626.md`.
+
+## Gap
+
+The external conjecture identifies an operational transition count with
+an arithmetic divisor transform. Its exact all-positive-input event is
+registered in issue [25808](https://github.com/the-omega-institute/trureturing/issues/25808),
+with the unchanged [prospective declaration](https://github.com/the-omega-institute/trureturing/issues/25808#issuecomment-6587694551).
+The formal bridge relates a restoring binary block to the arithmetic
+transform for all positive inputs.
+
+## Route
+
+A block of k zero bits followed by one and arbitrary higher cells admits
+a restoring trace. The recursive step composes two traversals of the
+smaller block and three literal transitions, giving T(0) = 1 and
+T(k+1) = 2 T(k) + 3, hence T(k) = 4·2^k − 3. Binary recursion finds this
+first one for every positive input. Independently, the published
+multiplicative Moebius and totient facts reduce the divisor transform to
+the same value: the odd factor contributes one and the power of two
+contributes 4·2^k − 3. Uniqueness of the initial zero block matches the two
+values, yielding the original signed sum and a genuine operational trace.
+
+## Falsifier
+
+Source fidelity would fail if the rule-number decoder, initial head,
+implicit blanks or counted boundary-crossing convention differed from the
+source. Under the stated semantics, a positive input whose actual first
+crossing count differs from the displayed divisor sum would contradict
+`D5/S0/Computability/BinaryMachine/Machine3626.result`. Agreement on a
+finite set of inputs alone cannot establish this universal claim.
+
+## Evidence
+
+The formal result is
+`D5/S0/Computability/BinaryMachine/Machine3626.result`.
+Its operational prerequisites are
+`D5/S0/Computability/BinaryMachine/Machine3626.block_first_crossing` and
+`D5/S0/Computability/BinaryMachine/Machine3626.positive_input_first_crossing`.
+The source-equivalence registrations are in
+`Reg/D5/S0/Computability/BinaryMachine/Machine3626.lean`; the Blueprint
+mirrors the source formula, integer casts and operational conventions.
+The primary rule decoder is WolframInstitute/TuringMachine commit
+`d23b7bcb741c711ea7b87a76391da1ac150c3bba`, `from_number` in
+`TuringMachine/Libs/ndtm_search/src/models.rs`, and initialization/counting
+are given by `OneSidedTuringMachineFunctionNative` in
+`TuringMachine/Kernel/Functions.wl`. The implementation's maxSteps
+parameter is not a hypothesis of the theorem.
+
+## Triage
+
+`theorem`; one source-qualified universal question with the aliases
+A393210 and A069517. The source author is Peter Bala; the source tier is 1.
+
+### What the settlement shows
+
+- Proved (`D5/S0/Computability/BinaryMachine/Machine3626.result`): every
+  positive binary input has an actual first-crossing trace whose count
+  equals the original signed Moebius/totient divisor sum. This proves the
+  displayed A393210 conjecture and the equivalent relation in A069517.
+- Proved (`D5/S0/Computability/BinaryMachine/Machine3626.block_first_crossing`):
+  arbitrary higher Boolean cells can replace the canonical higher binary
+  digits once the initial block is k zeros followed by one. The same exact
+  count 4·2^k − 3 applies without assumptions on those higher cells; the
+  restoring trace is the decisive mechanism.
+- Proved (`D5/S0/Computability/BinaryMachine/Machine3626.positive_input_first_crossing`):
+  every positive input has such a block. The count is an equality,
+  including the final crossing transition, rather than an upper bound.

+  The arithmetic multiplicativity and prime-power prerequisites remain

+- Open: input zero, other machines, other boundary or counting
+  conventions, and any further identities or classifications require
